newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar rises quietly, bonds firm after CPI data.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar rises quietly, bonds firm after CPI data.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar rose quietly and bond yields nudged down on Tuesday after the release of key inflation data for the June quarter.
Statistics New Zealand said at 10.45 a.m. that headline inflation rose 0.1 percent in the quarter and 1.1 percent in the June year.
The Reserve Bank of New Zealand used that data to calculate core inflation of 0.30 percent in the quarter and 1.49 percent in the year.
At 11.45 a.m. the kiwi dollar was quoted at US$0.6665/72, compared to US$0.6660/65 at the open, while on its Trade-Weighted Index the currency rose to 65.89 from 65.81 at the open.
The 90-day bank bill rate dipped back to 7.45 percent, after trading up to 7.48 percent before the release, while bond yields were narrowly lower than in the run-up to the data.

Monetary conditions tightened a touch, with the Monetary Conditions Index narrowing to 764. At that level conditions were 61 basis points (in interest rate terms) below the RBNZ's desired level, and seven points outside its comfort zone.
In early trade the MCI had been at 757.94, which was 67 points below the RBNZ's assumptions.
Economists had on average forecast core inflation of 0.3 percent for the quarter and 1.5 percent for the year, and the RBNZ had also picked quarterly core inflation of 0.3 percent.
